This Roman empress divorced her first husband to marry Octavian in 38 BC, and remained his wife when the Senate proclaimed him Augustus nine years later — who was she?
Livia (30 January 59 BC - AD 29) was Roman empress from 27 BC to AD 14 as the wife of Augustus, the first Roman emperor.

Merovingian dynasty was the ruling family of the Franks from around the middle of the 5th century until Pepin the Short in 751.

This giant huntsman of Greek myth was placed among the stars by Zeus or Artemis, and one legend even credits him with carving out the shape of the Strait of Sicily — who is he?
Orion (mythology) (: Ancient) was a giant huntsman whom Zeus or Artemis placed among the stars as a constellation.

MUMPS (published 1966) is the earliest of the four.
Who among these is a physicist?
John Tyndall is a physicist. John Tyndall (2 August 1820 – 4 December 1893) was an Irish physicist.
Which of these is a chemist?
Fritz Haber is a chemist. For this work, Haber has been called one of the most important scientists and industrial chemists in human history.
What is the atomic number of Aluminium?
Aluminium (the Commonwealth and preferred IUPAC name) or aluminum (North American English) is a chemical element; it has symbol Al and atomic number 13.
In what year was Johann Wolfgang von Goethe born?
Johann Wolfgang von Goethe (28 August 1749 – 22 March 1832) was a German polymath who is widely regarded as the most influential writer in the German language.
In what year was Oganesson discovered?
Oganesson is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Og and atomic number 118.
In what year was Arsenic discovered?
Arsenic is a chemical element; it has the symbol As and atomic number 33.
Indometacin: Pfizer. It works by inhibiting the production of prostaglandins, endogenous signaling molecules known to cause these symptoms.
In which country is Blood orange?
Blood orange: Italy. The blood orange is a variety of orange with crimson, near blood-colored flesh.
Who is credited with discovering Iodine?
Iodine: Bernard Courtois. Iodine is a chemical element; it has symbol I and atomic number 53.
Who is credited with discovering Mendelevium?
Mendelevium: Glenn Theodore Seaborg. Mendelevium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Md (formerly Mv) and atomic number 101.
Who is credited with discovering Magnesium?
Magnesium: Joseph Black. Magnesium is a chemical element; it has symbol Mg and atomic number 12.
This long-term skin condition occurs when dead skin cells and oil clog hair follicles, producing blackheads, whiteheads, and pimples mainly on the face, chest, and back — what is it?
Acne is a long-term skin condition that occurs when dead skin cells and sebum clog hair follicles.

This South African bulb genus tends to flower around March, earning a local nickname tied to that month, and is often confused with the Hippeastrum plants sold at Christmas under its common name — which genus?
Amaryllis is the only genus in the subtribe Amaryllidinae (tribe Amaryllideae).
Found only on male deer, except reindeer, this branching structure of bone and cartilage falls off and regrows from scratch each year — what is it?
Antler are extensions of an animal's skull found in members of the Cervidae (deer) family.

The third-largest member of its family behind the Siberian taimen and Pacific Chinook, this anadromous fish hatches in rivers, matures at sea, and changes color and appearance when it returns upstream to spawn — name this fish?
Atlantic salmon (Salmo salar) is a species of ray-finned fish in the family Salmonidae.
Usually the tenth-brightest star in the night sky, this red supergiant in the constellation Orion varies noticeably in brightness over a roughly 400-day cycle — name the star?
Betelgeuse is a red supergiant star in the equatorial constellation of Orion. Its Bayer designation is α Orionis, Latinised to Alpha Orionis and abbreviated Alpha Ori or α Ori.

Derived from Greek words for 'slow' and 'heart', this medical term describes a resting heart rate under 60 beats per minute — sometimes a red flag, sometimes just a sign of a well-conditioned athlete. Name the condition?
Bradycardia (brads), meaning "slow", and (karda), meaning "heart", also called bradyarrhythmia, is a resting heart rate under 60 beats per minute (BPM).
Caused by an overgrowth of a common yeast, this fungal infection is known as thrush when it affects the mouth and can also cause a genital yeast infection — name the condition?
Candidiasis is a fungal infection due to any species of yeasts in the genus Candida or those that were formerly classified in genus Candida but are now classified in the genus Candidozyma.
Also known by the taxonomic synonym Epilobium, this hardy perennial in the willowherb family is native throughout the temperate north — which plant?
Chamaenerion angustifolium is a perennial herbaceous flowering plant in the willowherb family, Onagraceae.
Its Latin genus name literally means three-leaf, and this herbaceous legume, native to Europe, now grows worldwide in around 300 species — what plant is it?
Clover are plants of the genus Trifolium (from Latin tres 'three' and folium 'leaf').

This naturally occurring but largely inactive steroid hormone shields organs like the kidneys from active cortisol, and gets converted back into cortisol by an enzyme mainly in the liver — what hormone is it?
Cortisone is a naturally occurring, mostly inactive pregnene (21-carbon) steroid hormone.
Affecting some 280 million people worldwide, this state of low mood saps motivation and the pleasure once taken in activities — what is it?
Depression (mood) is a mental state of low mood and aversion to activity.
Covering everything from a fibrous bone condition to a kidney disorder, this term for abnormal tissue growth is usually precancerous rather than outright malignant — what is it?

Dysplasia is any of various types of abnormal growth or development of cells (microscopic scale) or organs (macroscopic scale), and the abnormal histology or anatomical structure(s) resulting from such growth.
This thin, protective tissue type lines the outer surfaces of organs and the inner surfaces of blood vessels; the skin's outermost layer is a familiar example. What is it?
Epithelium is a thin, continuous, protective layer of cells with little extracellular matrix.

Likely domesticated from the European polecat, with which it can still interbreed, this slender Mustelid pet weighs up to about two kilograms and comes in coats of black, brown or white — which animal?
Ferret (Mustela furo) is a small, domesticated species belonging to the family Mustelidae.

This genus of scented flowering shrubs in the coffee family was named for an 18th-century naturalist, though Carl Linnaeus gets most of the credit over the botanist who first proposed it — which genus?
Gardenia is a genus of flowering plants in the coffee family, Rubiaceae, native to the tropical and subtropical regions of Africa, Asia, Madagascar, Pacific Islands, and Australia.
This large, semi-bitter citrus fruit originated in Barbados as an accidental 18th-century hybrid of the sweet orange and the pomelo, and has also been called the 'forbidden fruit.' What is it?
Grapefruit (Citrus paradisi) is a subtropical citrus tree known for its relatively large, sour to semi-sweet, somewhat bitter fruit.

Known as 'The Last Universalist' for mastering nearly every branch of his field, this French mathematician and physicist founded modern chaos theory through his study of the three-body problem — who is he?
Henri Poincaré (29 April 1854 - 17 July 1912) was a French mathematician, theoretical physicist, engineer, and philosopher of science.
A body-temperature emergency defined as a reading above 104°F, this condition kills roughly half a million people annually and is most commonly triggered by heat stroke — what is it called?
Hyperthermia is a condition in which an individual's body temperature is elevated beyond normal due to failed thermoregulation.

From deep-sea gribbles to the woodlice under your garden stones, members of this crustacean order share seven pairs of jointed limbs and brood their young in a pouch called a marsupium — what is the order?
Isopoda is an order of crustaceans. The order is divided into eleven suborders.
Famed first for studying diamagnetism, which Irish physicist proved in 1859 the link between atmospheric CO2 and what we now call the greenhouse effect?
John Tyndall (2 August 1820 - 4 December 1893) was an Irish physicist.

This genus of rod-shaped, gram-positive bacteria forms a significant part of the human microbiota in places like the digestive and genital tracts, and until a 2020 taxonomic overhaul included 261 distinct species — what's the genus?
Lactobacillus is a genus of gram-positive bacteria within the Lactobacillaceae family.
This common, soft, movable, painless growth made of fatty tissue usually forms just under the skin, often on the back, shoulders, or abdomen — name this benign tumor?
Lipoma is a benign tumor made of fat tissue. The first use of the term "lipoma" to describe these tumors was in 1709.

Located partly outside the body and partly within the pelvis, this set of sex organs includes the testicles, which produce sperm to fertilize an egg during conception — which body system is being described?
Male reproductive system consists of a number of sex organs that play a role in the process of human reproduction.
A waxy crystalline compound from peppermint and corn mint, it triggers a cooling sensation and works as a mild local anesthetic to soothe a sore throat — what is it?
Menthol is a monoterpenoid organic compound that occurs naturally in the oils of certain plants in the mint family, such as corn mint and peppermint.

Native to Africa, Asia, and Oceania, with one invasive species now in the southern U.S., this reptile genus ranges from 20 centimeters long to over 3 meters in the Komodo dragon — name this group of lizards?
Monitor lizard are lizards in the genus Varanus, the only extant genus in the family Varanidae.

Sometimes reaching two meters long but often thinner than a millimeter or two wide, these thread-like parasitoid worms turn up in damp puddles, troughs, and swimming pools as adults — what phylum is this?

Nematomorpha (sometimes called Gordiacea, and commonly known as horsehair worms, hairsnakes, or Gordian worms) are a phylum of parasitoid animals similar to yet distinct from nematode worms in morphology, hence the name.
Founder of the charity Volnoe Delo and the industrial group Basic Element, which Russian oligarch led both En+ Group and Rusal until stepping down in 2018?
Oleg Deripaska (born 2 January 1968) is a Russian oligarch and billionaire.

Closely related to carrot and parsley, this pale, long-tapered root vegetable grows sweeter in flavor after winter frosts and produces yellow flowers if left unharvested into its second season — name the vegetable?
Parsnip (Pastinaca sativa) is a root vegetable closely related to carrot and parsley, all belonging to the flowering plant family Apiaceae.
Prized as an ornamental indoor plant and still poorly understood taxonomically, this arum-family genus ranks second in size only to Anthurium — which genus?
Philodendron is a large genus of flowering plants in the family Araceae.
This birth defect results in extra fingers or toes, occurs more often in the hands than the feet, and has been linked to more than three dozen genetic mutations — what is it?
Polydactyly (commonly known as sixth finger and extra finger) is a birth defect that results in extra fingers or toes.

This psychiatric state describes an inability to distinguish reality from delusion, marked by symptoms like hallucinations and disorganized thinking, and can stem from conditions like schizophrenia or bipolar disorder — name the state?
Psychosis is the inability to distinguish what is or is not real.
This inflammatory disease typically develops two to four weeks after a streptococcal throat infection and can damage the heart valves in about half of cases — what is it?
Rheumatic fever (RF) is an inflammatory disease that can involve the heart, joints, skin, and brain.
After dropping out of Stanford and co-founding a startup later sold for over $40 million, this entrepreneur led Y Combinator before taking the helm of a leading AI company — who is he?
Sam Altman (born April 22, 1985) is an American entrepreneur and investor who has been the chief executive officer (CEO) of the artificial intelligence company OpenAI since 2019.
Cartilaginous and toothy, these fish are the sister group to the rays and skates and trace their ancestors to the Devonian Period — what are they?

Shark are a group of elasmobranch cartilaginous fishes characterized by a ribless endoskeleton, dermal denticles, five to seven gill slits on each side, and pectoral fins that are not fused to the head.
This birth defect involves incomplete closure of the spinal column and its surrounding membranes during early pregnancy, occurring in three recognized forms — what condition is it?
Spina bifida (SB; Latin for 'split spine') is a birth defect in which there is incomplete closing of the spine and the membranes around the spinal cord during early development in pregnancy.
Named for its long, flat, sword-like bill, this large migratory predatory fish loses all its teeth and scales by adulthood and is a popular target among billfish anglers — what is it?
Swordfish (Xiphias gladius), also known as the broadbill in some countries, are large, highly migratory predatory fish characterized by a long, flat, sword-like, pointed bill.

In 1933 he won the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for discoveries about the role of chromosomes in heredity, studying fruit-fly genetics after the rediscovery of Mendelian inheritance in 1900—who was this pioneering biologist?
Thomas Hunt Morgan (September 25, 1866 - December 4, 1945) was an American evolutionary biologist, geneticist, and embryologist.

These simple-looking marine invertebrates prove their kinship to vertebrates as larvae, when they sport a notochord, a dorsal nerve cord, and a post-anal tail — resembling a tiny tadpole. What are they?
Tunicate are marine invertebrates belonging to the subphylum Tunicata.
Named from a French verb meaning 'to see,' this term describes the practice of secretly watching others in intimate moments, often labeled 'Peeping Tom' behavior — what is it?
Voyeurism is the habit of clandestine watching other people engaged in intimate behaviors, such as undressing, sexual activity, or other actions of a private nature, commonly for sexual stimulation.

This Polish-American scholar served as Jimmy Carter's national security advisor from 1977 to 1981 and helped organize an influential international policy group known as the Trilateral Commission — who is he?
Zbigniew Brzezinski (March 28, 1928 - May 26, 2017) was a Polish-American diplomat and political scientist.
This term for cancer that begins in gland cells applies to the most common form of breast cancer and one of the two major types of esophageal cancer — which term?
De Havilland Canada DHC-6 Twin Otter
Adenocarcinoma: Cancer of epithelial cells with glandular origin or characteristics.

Often called the greatest mathematician of the twentieth century, this German-born Frenchman revolutionized algebraic geometry before abruptly leaving his post at a Paris research institute in 1970 — who is he?

These coiled-shelled cephalopods, more closely related to octopuses than to nautiluses despite the resemblance, thrived from the Devonian until vanishing around the dinosaur extinction 66 million years ago — what are they?
Ammonoidea: Extinct subclass of cephalopod molluscs.
Known by the symbol Sb and mined chiefly from stibnite ore, which element has long been powdered into the cosmetic kohl and today hardens lead in car batteries?
Antimony: Chemical element with atomic number 51 (Sb)
His namesake effect — scattered X-rays losing energy — proved light behaves as particles and earned a share of the 1927 Nobel Prize in Physics. Who was this American physicist?
Discovered by Robert Koch in 1876, this rod-shaped microbe was the first ever shown experimentally to cause disease, providing the earliest evidence for germ theory — which organism?

With his former teacher Alfred North Whitehead, this English philosopher co-wrote Principia Mathematica and, alongside G. E. Moore, led the British 'revolt against idealism.' Who was this founder of analytic philosophy?
Bertrand Russell: English mathematician and philosopher (1872–1970)
Conceived for Pan Am as a jet two-and-a-half times the size of the 707, this wide-body, led by designer Joe Sutter, rolled out of the world's largest building in 1968 — which airliner is it?
Boeing 747: American wide-body four-engined jet long-range aircraft.
Often called a 'chest cold,' this inflammation of the airways typically causes a cough lasting around three weeks and is usually caused by a virus?
Bronchitis: Inflammation of the large airways in the lungs.
Bearing distinctive fatty humps and used for milk, meat, and transport across deserts for millennia, which ungulate comes in a common one-humped form and a rarer two-humped form?
Its raw shell and seed are actually toxic until roasted or steamed, and the tropical American tree it grows on also yields a fleshy 'apple' — what is this familiar snack?
Cashew: Flowering plant in the family Anacardiaceae.
Also known as christophine or mirliton, this gourd-family fruit was first cultivated in Mesoamerica and is often cooked like summer squash — what is it?
Chayote: Edible fruiting vine of the gourd family.

An American naturalist who surveyed wildlife in Labrador, he turned his observations into quick-freezing methods that launched the modern frozen food industry — and a famous brand bears his name. Who was he?
Clarence Birdseye: American inventor, entrepreneur, and naturalist.
Widespread across Europe, Asia, and Africa, this small predatory falcon has occasionally strayed as far as Guam and the U.S. east coast — what bird is it?
Common kestrel: Species of bird. In the United Kingdom, where no other kestrel species commonly occurs, it is generally just called the "kestrel".
Which tart fruit ripens on trailing evergreen vines with dark pink flowers, turning from light green to red as it matures?
Cranberry: Group of plant species bearing edible fruit.
Originally developed as an antidepressant, this fast-acting SSRI was later approved to treat premature ejaculation and was sold to Johnson & Johnson in 2003 — what drug is it?
Dapoxetine: Medication used to treat premature ejaculation.
Marketed as Lanoxin, this centuries-old heart medication boosts contraction strength while slowing the heart rate, but can cause blurred vision and breast enlargement in excess — what is it?
Marked by itchy 1-2mm blisters on the palms and soles that clear in three to four weeks but often return, this form of dermatitis has no known cause — what is it?
Dyshidrosis: Inflammatory disease of the skin in humans.

Often tangled up with mood, temperament, and creativity, these neurophysiological states carry a degree of pleasure or displeasure — yet scientists still can't agree on a single definition. What are they?
Dubbed the 'father of geometry,' this ancient Greek mathematician's treatise Elements dominated the field for nearly two thousand years — who is he?
Found on birds and even some non-avian dinosaurs, this complex evolutionary structure aids flight, insulation and waterproofing, and gives its name to the study of plumology — what is it?
Despite the name, these fifty species of rodent can't truly fly — they glide between trees using a furred membrane called a patagium. What are they?
Caused by a loss of blood supply and marked by skin turning red or black, this condition comes in dry, wet, and gas forms — what is it?
Gangrene: Type of tissue death by ischemia.

Inducted into the U.S. Air Force Hall of Fame in 2018, this American mathematician modeled the precise shape of the Earth — work later baked into the Global Positioning System that now guides your phone. Who is she?
Rising from the ashes of the cancelled F-111B, which variable-sweep-wing Navy fighter first flew in 1970 and deployed aboard USS Enterprise?
Grumman F-14 Tomcat: Carrier-based multi-role fighter aircraft family.
A 1930s-40s Hollywood star of films like Algiers, she also co-invented a radio guidance system during WWII — which glamorous on-screen inventor was she?
Hedy Lamarr: Austrian-American actress and inventor (1914–2000)
Known as the great apes, this primate family holds eight living species across four genera — orangutans, gorillas, chimps and bonobos, plus one more: us. What is it?
Hominidae: Family of primates. The original meaning of "hominid" referred only to humans (Homo) and their closest extinct relatives.

Responsible for nearly half a million deaths each year, this condition occurs when the body produces or absorbs more heat than it can dissipate, most often from heat stroke or a drug reaction — what condition?
Hyperthermia: Elevated body temperature due to failed thermoregulation.
This concept in calculus, a continuous analog of a sum, computes the signed area under a curve and pairs with differentiation as one of the field's two fundamental operations?
This fragrant genus of shrubs and vines in the olive family is grown in vast quantities in one Egyptian village that supplies much of the world's perfume industry — which plant?
Jasmine: Genus of flowering plant in the olive family Oleaceae.
Born Giulia Maddalena Angela in Italy, this physician became a leading freethinker and activist for women's rights and social reform in early-20th-century Argentina — who is she?
Julieta Lanteri: Argentine doctor and activist (1873–1932)

Ranked alongside Aristotle and Frege among history's most significant logicians, this thinker proved his completeness theorem in his 1929 Vienna dissertation before publishing his famous incompleteness theorems two years later — who is he?
Kurt Gödel: Mathematical logician and philosopher.

Originally cultivated by the ancient Egyptians and now grown worldwide with China producing over half the crop, this leafy Asteraceae vegetable also has a stem-focused variety called celtuce — name the vegetable?
Lettuce: Species of annual plant of the daisy family, most often grown as a leaf vegetable.
Genus name meaning 'horned' in Latin, this raptor nests in dense woodland edges but hunts over open ground, feeding mostly on voles — which bird?
Long-eared owl: Species of owl. The genus name, Asio, is Latin for "horned owl", and the specific epithet, otus, is derived from Greek and refers to a small eared owl.
Domesticated some 9,000 years ago in southern Mexico from a wild grass called teosinte, this tall stout grain was once planted beside beans and squash in the Three Sisters trio — what is it?
Maize: Species of grass cultivated as a food crop.

First flown in August 1970 and introduced by American Airlines the following year, this trijet wide-body aircraft has two underwing engines and a third mounted at the base of its tail fin — which aircraft?
McDonnell Douglas DC-10: Wide-body three-engine airliner.
Sold under the brand name Medrol, this synthetic steroid can trigger iatrogenic Cushing's syndrome if not carefully tapered after high-dose use for acute flares — name the drug?

An Egyptian-born civil engineer and architect who studied in Cairo and Germany, at 33 he was the oldest of the 19 hijackers and the ringleader who piloted American Airlines Flight 11 into the North Tower — who was he?
Mohamed Atta: Egyptian terrorist and 9/11 hijacker (1968–2001)
One of the smallest self-replicating organisms known, this cell-wall-lacking bacterium was originally called the 'Eaton agent' after being cultivated in chicken eggs in 1944 — what organism is it?
Mycoplasma pneumoniae: Species of bacterium. Mycoplasma pneumoniae is a species of very small-cell bacteria that lack a cell wall, in the class Mollicutes.
This British-American historian, a senior fellow at Stanford's Hoover Institution, writes on financial history and holds notably favorable views of the British Empire — who is he?
First described by Linnaeus in 1758, this medium-sized spotted wild cat hunts armadillos and opossums at twilight across a range from the southwestern US to South America — what cat is it?
Ocelot: Species of wild cat. It is native to the southwestern United States, Mexico, Central and South America, and the Caribbean islands of Trinidad and Margarita.

Triggered by a surge of luteinizing hormone near the midpoint of the menstrual cycle, this event sees the ovarian follicle rupture and release an egg — which breaks down in under a day if it isn't fertilized. What is it called?
Ovulation: Release of egg cells from the ovaries.
One of the 20th century's most prolific mathematicians, this Hungarian championed Ramsey theory and famously preferred cracking open problems to building grand theories — who was he?

Approved for medical use in the US back in 1959 and sold under the brand name Adipex-P, this appetite-suppressing stimulant is a substituted amphetamine used alongside diet and exercise to treat obesity — what is it?

There are exactly five of these convex regular polyhedra — tetrahedron, cube, octahedron, dodecahedron, and icosahedron — named for the philosopher who linked them to the classical elements. What are they called?
Platonic solid: Any of the five regular polyhedra. In geometry, a Platonic solid is a convex, regular polyhedron in three-dimensional Euclidean space.
This legal document spells out how a business collects, stores, and shares personal details like your address, financial records, or medical history — what is it called?
Privacy policy: Management of personal data across media.
Recognizable by its bold red-and-black pattern, this true bug is often confused with the unrelated cinnamon bug and forms large aggregations across Europe and Asia — which species is it?
Pyrrhocoris apterus: Species of true bug. The firebug, Pyrrhocoris apterus, is a common insect of the family Pyrrhocoridae.
Scholars call it an "essentially contested concept" with no agreed definition, but it broadly links humanity to the supernatural through behaviors, ethics, texts and sacred places — what is it?
This enormous flowering-plant family, named for its type genus, gives us apples, cherries, strawberries, and ornamental roses alike — which plant family is it?
Rosaceae: Rose family of flowering plants.
A former finance minister and central bank board member, this economist became the 52nd president of Paraguay in 2023 after switching from a liberal party to the Colorado Party — who is he?
Santiago Peña: President of Paraguay since 2023. Peña served on leadership boards for the Central Bank of Paraguay and Banco Amambay.
About 90% of this mood-regulating neurotransmitter is actually made in your gut, where it controls intestinal movement, rather than the brain — also known as 5-HT, what is it?
Serotonin: Monoamine neurotransmitter. It is involved in mood, cognition, reward, learning, memory, and physiological processes such as vomiting and vasoconstriction.
The sixth most abundant element in Earth's crust, this soft alkali metal carries symbol Na and pairs with chlorine as the ocean's most common dissolved element — what is it?
Sodium: Chemical element with atomic number 11 (Na)
Named in 1880 from Greek words meaning 'bunch of grapes,' this genus of spherical, grape-clustered bacteria can grow with or without oxygen — which genus?
Striking suddenly and resolving — one way or another — within 8 to 10 hours, this mysterious epidemic first hit England in 1485 and vanished after a final outbreak in 1551 — what was it called?
Sweating sickness: Contagious disease in Europe, 1485–1551.
An Australian-American math prodigy who won the Fields Medal in 2006, he proved a famous theorem on prime numbers with Ben Green in 2004. Who is he?
Terence Tao: Australian and American mathematician (born 1975)

Proposing an information-management system in March 1989, this English computer scientist implemented the first web browser and web server and founded the organization that still oversees the web's standards — who is he?
Feeding exclusively on vertebrate blood across tropical Africa, this biting fly folds its wings completely over its abdomen at rest and spreads trypanosomiasis — which insect?
Tsetse fly: Genus of disease-spreading insects.

Discovered in 1801 by a Spanish-Mexican scientist but only confirmed as a new element in 1830, this hard silvery-grey transition metal takes its name from a Scandinavian goddess of beauty — what element is it?
Vanadium: Chemical element with atomic number 23 (V)
Equal to seven days, this standard calendrical period sits between a single day and a month — despite ancient Egyptians preferring a ten-day version, what unit of time is it?
Week: Time unit equal to seven days. The days of the week are often used to set work days, rest days, and holy days.
With atomic number 39, this silvery metal is chemically similar to the lanthanides, never occurs freely in nature, and once gave old CRT televisions their red phosphor glow — which element?
Yttrium: Chemical element with atomic number 39 (Y)
What is the chemical symbol for rhodium?
The symbol for rhodium is Rh. Rhodium is a chemical element; it has symbol Rh and atomic number 45.
What is the chemical symbol for indium?
The symbol for indium is In. Indium is a chemical element; its symbol is In and its atomic number is 49.

Fran Drescher: Francine Joy Drescher (born September 30, 1957) is an American actress, writer, comedian, producer, and former trade union leader.

Chuck Norris: Carlos Ray "Chuck" Norris (March 10, 1940 – March 19, 2026) was an American martial artist, actor, screenwriter, and author.

In what year was Robert Redford born?
Robert Redford: Redford began his career on television in the late 1950s, appearing in anthology series such as Alfred Hitchcock Presents and The Twilight Zone.

Civil War (film): With a budget of $50 million, Civil War was A24's most expensive film at the time.
